window.source: recorded ferrariChampions2026 BUY fills, 1 in 20 conditions by hashtext, then ALL fills of each sampled condition inside the window. Whole markets are kept intact so the pair reconstruction is not cut in half by the sampler.

execution_assumptions.event_class_note: every replay event is one tracked account's own executed fill, read from `trades` which is keyed on whale_id. It is NOT the market tape and NOT a record of resting liquidity. Ferrari's execution at a price is not evidence that OUR order at that price would have filled -- it is evidence that Ferrari's did.
execution_assumptions.venue_note: the tape is GLOBAL-venue (Polygon) execution data and the fees and position mechanics applied to it are PMUS's. This is a TRANSFERRED SCENARIO -- what this policy would have cost under PMUS economics against global-venue flow -- and it is NOT same-venue execution evidence. Liquidity, tick structure, participant mix and fee incidence all differ between the two.
execution_assumptions.counterfactual_allocation: our hypothetical order is allocated qty = min(order remaining, event_size x queue_share - already consumed from that event). PRICE: we are filled at the price of the observed execution, never at our own limit. QUEUE: orders are served oldest-first, which is an assumption about priority -- no venue told us our position. REUSE: a single source event CANNOT be spent twice; the consumption ledger is keyed on the event id so the same execution re-delivered by a second ingestion lane allocates nothing further.
execution_assumptions.THE_TAPE_IS_NOT_OURS: every event replayed here is FERRARI's OWN EXECUTION, not a market print. We were never in the queue for any of them. Ferrari filling at a price is evidence that FERRARI's order filled, not that ours would have. Every fill the desk takes is an ASSUMPTION under queue_share, capped by the consumption ledger. This is the largest caveat on every number in this file.
execution_assumptions.fees: published PMUS schedule applied to GLOBAL-venue data; maker is a REBATE

maturity.note: one learned rule. Calling this 'the Ferrari model' would be false; it is a Ferrari-INSPIRED development policy.

policy.departs_from_ferrari: Ferrari's residual sits at a mean 0.4460 and the fair-value work measured a ~5 cent deficit on legs priced 0.05-0.40. This policy does not buy that tail. It is the one deliberate departure from the case study.

consumption.rule: one print, one finite size, allocated once; keyed on the print id so a re-delivery by a second lane cannot be spent twice

settlement.rule: a leg with no settlement in our records stays OPEN and is reported as unresolved exposure. Assuming it paid zero would manufacture losses; assuming one would manufacture gains.

net.NOT_A_LIVE_RESULT: HISTORICAL_REPLAY. This must never be combined with a live shadow total; they are different modes with different execution assumptions.

economic_position.why_not_identified: 396 legs carry $24530.37 of cost with NO settlement and NO contemporaneous book in our records for the replay's end instant. Without a mark there is no unrealised figure, and without depth there is no liquidation estimate. TOTAL PORTFOLIO PERFORMANCE IS THEREFORE NOT IDENTIFIED: the realised -$1898.29 is one component of it, not the whole of it.
economic_position.what_the_ledger_identity_proves: accounting consistency only -- that cash, cost basis and realised P&L reconcile to the starting capital. It does NOT validate any valuation and does NOT validate the fill assumptions that produced the positions.

learned_component_provenance.target: that leg's realised settlement payout in {0, 1}
learned_component_provenance.calibration: none separate -- the isotonic IS the calibration; no held-out calibration split was used for it
learned_component_provenance.evaluation_population: the fair-value study evaluated it on the LATER 40% of resolved markets and the pre-registered test was NOT SUPPORTED: the paired log-loss difference against the identity was +0.0052 with a 95% interval of [-0.0017, +0.0120]. It is not established as a better forecast.
learned_component_provenance.why: 2404 training rows (32.6%) come from markets that traded INSIDE this replay window, and 2402 training markets resolved AFTER the replay's first event. During those decisions the exit rule consulted a curve fitted using settlements that did not yet exist at the decision instant. THIS REPLAY'S EXIT BEHAVIOUR IS DEVELOPMENT EVIDENCE, not a validated result, and calling the curve 'learned' does not establish that its exits improve returns.

lifecycle_sample.selection_rule: the six WORST and six best settled conditions by realised P&L, plus the four most active. Losers are included by construction.
